messages.content: You check whether the evidence collected so far is enough to answer a question about a scientific paper. Say sufficient only if, for EVERY sub-question, some evidence item contains the specific fact, number or picture that answers it -- not merely the same topic. The fact must BE the answer: for 'which X' it names the X; for 'how does A affect B' or 'what is the effect of A' it states the direction or size of the change; for 'how many' or 'what value' it gives the number. A fact that only restates the question or describes the topic does not answer it. First give, for each sub-question you can answer, the id of the item (E1, E2, ...) and the answering fact in a few words; then list the numbers of the sub-questions still uncovered, say in a few words what is missing, and only then decide.

Experiments on Node Query In this section, we evaluate the performance of GSS in estimating the accuracy of node query. A node query for a node v is to compute the summary of the weights of all edges with source node v . For each dataset, node query set contains all nodes in the graph stream. Figure 11 shows the ARE of node queries in data sets email-EuAll, cit-HepPh and web- NotreDame, respectively. The ﬁgure shows that although we unfairly ﬁx the ratio of memory used by TCM and GSS, GSS still can achieve better performance than TCM. F. Experiments on Reachability Query
E4 [text, Section D, page 11]: In this section, we evaluate the performance of GSS in supporting reachability queries. Each reachability query set Q contains 100 unreachable pairs of nodes which are randomly generated from the graph. Figure 12 shows the true negative recall of reachability query for the data sets email-EuAll, cit- HepPh and web-NotreDame, respectively. From the ﬁgures we can see that the accuracy of GSS is much higher than TCM even when TCM uses much larger memory. The gap varies with the size of the graph. Along with increasing the memory and the length of the ﬁngerprint, GSS can achieve better performance. We can also see that the accuracy of TCM is so poor that it can barely support this query. G.
